backlog.spec: In the first SLSQP stage of each random restart, write the centre coordinates as a smooth combination of a small number of cosine basis functions over the unit square (for example 3 by 3 modes per coordinate, so about 18 coefficients). Fit the initial coefficients to a random target layout by least squares, then optimise the coefficients and radii with SLSQP. Afterwards, release the full 2n centre variables and run the usual _optimise to polish. This gives a smooth, low-dimensional global search before the full problem.
backlog.title: Low-dimensional Fourier-basis parametrisation for the first solve

backlog.spec: In each random restart, draw a random Gaussian matrix B of size (2n, d) with d around 3n, and optimise the variables v = v0 + B z together with the radii, using SLSQP on the reduced variables z (radii stay full-dimensional). After this stage, map back to the full centre vector and run the usual full _optimise to polish. The random projection reduces the number of constraint gradients per iteration and changes the basin that SLSQP reaches from a given start.
backlog.title: Random-subspace SLSQP in the first stage

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed MAX_ITER in the random-restart phase with a Luby-sequence schedule. Restart number k gets a maxiter equal to base * luby(k), where luby(k) is the standard Luby sequence (1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 2, 4, ...) and base is about 40. Keep the full MAX_ITER for the final remove-and-reinsert polishing. This gives many cheap restarts and a few long ones, without needing a per-restart stopping rule.
backlog.title: Luby-sequence restart budgets

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve in the remove-and-reinsert loop, estimate the Lagrange multipliers of the active pair and wall constraints. Do this by solving a non-negative least-squares problem: the objective gradient equals the sum of multipliers times constraint gradients, over constraints with slack below 1e-6. Score each circle by the sum of multipliers of its active constraints. Remove the circle with the smallest score (the one least stressed by the packing) instead of the smallest radius, and reinsert it into the largest hole. This is a principled version of the rattler heuristic.
backlog.title: NNLS multiplier-guided removal

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centres in _solve_once with points from a 2D Halton sequence (bases 2 and 3). Apply a random digit permutation per dimension, drawn from the seed, so each restart gets a different scrambled set. Map the points into [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW] and add a small random jitter of 0.01 to break exact lattice alignment. Keep the rest of the restart unchanged. This gives more even coverage of the square at the start than iid uniform sampling.
backlog.title: Halton low-discrepancy starts with random digit scrambling

backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, compute the contact graph of the incumbent (pairs whose distance minus radius sum is below 1e-6, plus wall contacts). Pick a random contact edge (i, j) that shares a neighbour with another contact, then move the centres of i and j to the two free positions that complete the adjacent triangle (the other common-neighbour arrangement). Re-solve with _optimise and _repair, and accept only if the radius sum improves. This explores neighbouring contact topologies rather than just relocating one small circle.
backlog.title: Contact-graph edge flip moves

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, draw a random aspect factor a from [0.7, 1.4] per restart. Optimise in scaled variables (x * a, y / a) with SLSQP for the first MAX_ITER/2 iterations, using the scaled wall constraints. Undo the scaling by mapping the centres back to the unit square and clipping, then run the usual _optimise polish on the unscaled problem. The distorted start changes which packings SLSQP reaches while the final solve remains exact.
backlog.title: Anisotropic stretch of search variables in the first stage

backlog.spec: Add a start generator that runs a short hard-disk Monte Carlo at a rising pressure. Start with n random centres and tiny radii. At each sweep, propose random displacements of each centre, and accept a move if it keeps the centre inside the square and does not overlap any disk of radius r. Between sweeps, raise every radius by a factor that depends on the acceptance rate, so that the packing grows toward jamming. After about 300 sweeps, pass the centres and radii to _optimise. Use this generator in about one third of the restarts.
backlog.title: Pressure-ramped hard-disk Monte Carlo start

incumbent.description: Grow about half of the random restarts from 4 circles to n by inserting each new zero-radius circle at the emptiest of 2000 sampled points, re-optimising after each insertion, and keep the best packing as the start of the remove-and-reinsert loop.

memo:
Helped: constructive insertion moves. Slot 0 (remove and reinsert the smallest circle) gave -0.0031. Slot 47 (grow about half the restarts from 4 circles to n by insertion) is the incumbent at -2.6347 (runs -2.6348/-2.6346, delta -0.0036).

Did not help: most single-run tweaks moved the loss by about ±0.0002. These include radii inits, wall placement, time fraction 0.9, early stopping and LP repair. Hurt: basin hopping (+0.0030), position screening (+0.0023), sparse constraints (+0.0021), ring starts (+0.0037), mirror starts (+0.0036), greedy-hole starts (+0.0030), quadrant starts (+0.0060).

Noise sd is 0.0023, so single runs mislead. Slots 57 and 65 each scored -2.6360 once but were rejected.

Next: stack near-misses on slot 47 and replicate each at least twice. Candidates: slot 18 annealing acceptance, slot 4 Latin hypercube starts, slot 30 hex/uniform alternation, slot 32 analytic gradients, slot 57 rotated lattice starts and slot 65 staged SLSQP. Also try a larger share of insertion-growth restarts.
